five_second.sells: Online courses that use drawing/pattern-art as a mindfulness and manifesting practice - not physical art supplies, actual video courses and a membership
five_second.for_whom: creative-minded people looking for a calming self-development or healing practice, seems aimed mostly at women into wellness/spirituality
five_second.price_guess: guessing somewhere around $30-80 per course, maybe $20-30/month for the membership

features_used.moment: scrolled through five course cards (Art of Manifesting, Membership, Sacred Geometry, Pattern Drawing, Chakra-Based Art) one by one
tapped it once and nothing visibly opened, had to tap a second time before the full menu slid in
opened the blog from the menu and a headline about calming pattern drawing grabbed me immediately, like the reel that brought me here
read a good chunk of the post in bed, it felt personal and genuinely soothing, not just sales copy
ran into three separate email-for-10%-off boxes baked right into the scroll on the homepage and blog post, ignored all of them per my own rule

features_used.feature: dedicated course sales page (Zendala Drawing Course)
features_used.moment: clicked through hoping to finally see a price, got a long JOIN NOW landing page with a teacher bio instead

features_looked_for_but_missing: an actual price shown on the homepage course cards
a real dollar number anywhere before multiple screens of scrolling
a simple way to save/bookmark a course for later without typing an email
feature_that_most_helped_the_decision: the Zendala Drawing blog post - it read like something a real person wrote at midnight for someone like me, which made the whole site feel worth a daylight revisit
feature_that_most_hurt_the_decision: the total absence of visible pricing - not on the homepage cards, not in the blog's course pitch (just 'special introductory price'), not in the first three screens of the actual course sales page

friction.moment: hamburger menu needed a second tap before the menu actually opened
scrolled all five homepage course cards top to bottom and never saw a single price
the blog post teased a 'special introductory price' with zero actual number, then the dedicated course page still had no visible price after three scrolls
three separate email-capture boxes appeared unprompted while just casually scrolling, none were popups but the repetition felt naggy

delight.moment: the 'Nice to meet you' section with Anna's own bio made the site feel like one real person's life work, not a template
reading the Zendala blog post about calm pattern drawing felt genuinely soothing for an 11:40pm phone-in-bed scroll, exactly the mood the reel promised

what_earned_it: a named, visible founder with her own bio and story
a real blog with a personal, caring voice instead of generic marketing copy
consistent niche and look across every page (same logo, palette, and tone)
trust.what_it_would_take: show me one real price on the first screen I see, and let me save something for later without handing over my email

brand_recall.tell_a_friend_one_sentence: It's this small, personal site run by a woman named Anna who teaches drawing-as-mindfulness and manifesting courses - kind of spiritual, but weirdly calming to scroll through at night.
